title: Autonomous Lean 4 Disproof of Smale’s 1981 Mean Value Conjecture (K = 1)
aiSystem: Pre-Release GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI / Epoch AI LeanOpenProblems)
whyItMatters: In Epoch AI’s autonomous evaluation over Formal Conjectures’ Wikipedia open problems, pre-release GPT-6 Astra disproved Steve Smale’s 1981 Mean Value Conjecture (K = 1) in Lean 4 with zero human guidance.
summary: In the same September 3, 2026 Epoch AI LeanOpenProblems evaluation that disproved the Köthe conjecture (github.com/tadamcz/mean-value-problem), a pre-release version of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra autonomously disproved the K = 1 form of Fields Medalist Steve Smale’s 1981 Mean Value Conjecture—a classic 45-year-old problem in complex analysis motivated by the complexity of Newton’s root-finding method. With zero human steering, GPT-6 Astra constructed a complex polynomial p with p(0) = 0, p′(0) = 1, and |p(c)/c| > 1 at every critical point c, formalizing the exact negation of DeepMind’s Formal Conjectures statement in Lean 4 + Mathlib with Comparator verification. The breakthrough spurred rapid follow-up work on Hexagon in November 2026, lowering the rigorously certified counterexample degree down to 2,799.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously disproved Steve Smale’s 1981 Mean Value Conjecture (K = 1) in Lean 4 + Mathlib with zero human intervention.
Exact negation of Formal Conjectures’ MeanValueProblem statement verified in an isolated Comparator container under standard axioms only.
Catalyzed November 2026 follow-up machine-certified counterexamples reducing polynomial degree down to 7,299 and 2,799.
caveats: Disproves the classic K = 1 bound in Smale’s conjecture; subsequent November 2026 Hexagon preprints examine the exact sharp constant (proposed as 4) and await peer review.
